title: Implement ordinary non-local delegation lifecycle

intent.outcome: Satisfy #2763 by proving one transport-neutral, revision-bound non-local assignment through selection, export/dispatch, returned-result admission, integration/proof, reconciliation, and next decision, including one real supported-host episode and automatic/manual parity.
non_goals: Do not add a provider-specific scheduler, second assignment packet, transcript store, durable worker registry, or new root command.
Do not let a worker self-authorize proof, integration, merge, closeout, scope widening, or parent completion.
Do not change the quiet direct-local path when local execution remains the canonical best fit.

parent.contribution: Completes the delegation-specific composed scenario required by #2562 after the #2762 enforcement ratchet.
parent.closure_boundary: This slice may close only #2763; parent #2562 and dogfooding parent #2721 remain for the final stacked closeout layer.

Returned work remains untrusted evidence until current assignment, target, scope, proof, stop-condition, and mutation-baseline authorities admit it.
A real supported-host read-only assignment records dispatch, return, admission, integration/proof, continuation lineage, and cost without storing raw transcript history.

next_action: Commit and publish the independently re-reviewed delegation lifecycle repair PR; merge it before reconciling #2763 and advancing the parent lane.
blockers: The canonical proof executor rejects the route-selected requirement-grounding command before launch because its authority still emits a literal <paths> placeholder; concrete execution passed, but completion remains claim-blocked until that route defect is repaired or explicitly escalated.

claims: An ordinary task can select one current non-local target under binding best-fit policy without explicit delegation wording and cannot silently fall back to local implementation.
Automatic and manual transports preserve one assignment identity and return contract; malformed, stale, wrong-target, out-of-scope, or authority-widening returns fail closed.
A valid worker return remains evidence until orchestrator-owned admission, integration, proof, and next-decision reconciliation succeed.
One real supported-host episode and its cost comparison prove the lifecycle without creating provider-specific semantic authority.
requirements: Run focused assignment lifecycle, operating-decision, composed-scenario, weak-worker, transport-parity, and quiet-local tests.
Run operation conformance, external consumer readiness, generated package parity, lint, typecheck, contract tooling, and runtime ownership checks.
Record a compact supported-host dogfood trace whose identities and receipts can be checked without raw transcript storage.
refs: Independent current-head review after PR #2778 merge: structural proof/task-proof confusion; read-only implement mutation; export-only automatic dispatch; premature assignment close; same-class assignment identity collision; keyword-derived mutation authority.
All first- and second-review findings repaired across canonical Python, native TypeScript, generated mirrors, operation contracts, and lifecycle tests.

proof.summary: The bounded repair is implementation-complete and independently re-reviewed with no findings. Local validation passed: 532 focused tests, 299 conformance passes with zero failures, generated-package checks, schema docs, lint, and typecheck. Canonical proof execution remains honestly claim-blocked by an unresolved literal <paths> template in the selected requirement-grounding route, so the slice remains open through PR merge, route repair or structured escalation, and #2763 reconciliation.

continuation.residual_intent: After this lane, reconcile #2562, #2721, #2752, and #2754 in the final stacked parent-closeout layer.
